description: Editorial description of the on-screen teaching sequence; not spoken narration. The soundtrack is music.

segments.text: Training adjusts the Transformer to predict the next character from preceding context.
Targets are the input stream shifted by one character. A batch of 32 windows with 64 positions provides 2,048 target predictions.
Teacher forcing supplies known previous tokens during training. A causal mask allows all positions to be trained in parallel without revealing their future answers.
Cross-entropy is minus the natural logarithm of the probability assigned to the correct next token. Average it over the prediction positions.
Judge loss against baselines. In this reference run, uniform guessing scores 4.174; frequency-based and previous-letter baselines are stronger comparisons.
The training toolkit includes AdamW, learning-rate warmup, cosine decay and gradient clipping.
Warmup increases the learning rate initially; decay reduces it later. Clipping limits a gradient norm when it exceeds the selected threshold.
Short learning-rate trials compare validation loss. The chosen 0.01 is specific to this small model and experiment.
The main reference run improves validation loss to about 1.742 in 1,400 steps. Perplexity exp(1.742) is approximately 5.7, not an accuracy percentage.
Compare selected predictions before and after training to see how context can improve the probability of a plausible next character.
Changing the available context length tests how much the trained model benefits from preceding characters.
Average attention weights visualize where this model mixes information, but do not by themselves establish causal explanations.
Pause: is a validation loss of 2.5 impressive if the previous-letter baseline already scores 2.482? Why can training evaluate 64 positions together?
A loss of 2.5 does not beat that baseline. Known targets plus causal masking make parallel teacher-forced training possible.
Recap training and evaluation. Continue to section 8 of this lesson to see how generation differs: predict a token, append it, and repeat.
